answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with bonded, time-vested identity. Every agent locks a refundable deposit before it can transact, and like a tide that only rises slowly, its spending limit grows only as it accumulates verified, paid work over weeks. A prism of checks — deposit size, work history, and peer attestations — scores each identity, so a single operator spinning up a falcon-swift army of fakes must fund every identity separately and wait out the same slow vesting for each one. The attacker's cost becomes linear in the number of identities, while honest agents pay only once.
